slides.headline: Credit means getting something [[now]] and paying for it [[later]].
You want $100 sneakers, but you only have [[$20]].

steps.title: You take the sneakers home
steps.sub: You leave the store with them today.

steps.title: The bank pays the store $100
steps.sub: The store gets paid in full.

steps.title: Later, you pay the bank back

slides.label: THE CATCH
slides.headline: Credit isn't free.
slides.sub: The bank charges a fee for lending you money. It's called [[interest]].
slides.note: Example uses 20% interest for one year with nothing repaid. Real rates vary.

slides.headline: Your [[credit score]] is your reliability grade.
slides.sub: A number lenders check to see if you repay on time.

rows.text: Repay on time: score up, loans cheaper
Repay late: score down, loans pricier

slides.note: Scoring systems differ from country to country.

slides.title: Credit = Trust
slides.sub: Someone trusts you to pay them back later.
checks: Get it now, **pay it back later**
Paying on time builds your **credit score**
